items.question: TD's net income jumped in fiscal 2025. How big was the jump and what explains it?
items.answer:
- How big: TD reported net income of C$20,538 million in 2025 versus C$8,842 million in 2024 [F1, S1]. The absolute increase was C$11,696 million (C$20,538m − C$8,842m) [F1, S1]. - What explains it (drivers cited in the filings):
  - Higher total revenue, driven by higher net interest income and much stronger non‑interest income in U.S. Retail and Corporate: total revenue rose to C$67,777m in 2025 from C$57,223m in 2024, with net interest income up (C$33,062m vs C$30,472m) and non‑interest income up (C$34,715m vs C$26,751m) — see the segment results table [S3].
  - A large increase in items included in non‑interest income in 2025 (notably higher gains in derivatives/hedging and Corporate items): see the large increase in “Net change in gain/(loss) on derivatives designated as cash flow hedges” and other OCI reclassifications in the consolidated statement (page 13) and the higher non‑interest income in the segment table [S1, S3].

  - A lower effective income tax rate in 2025 (reported effective tax rate 14.4% vs 24.8% last year) primarily reflecting the tax impact of the sale of Schwab shares in the current year and the absence of the prior‑year non‑deductible global resolution charges; total provision for income taxes rose in dollars but the effective rate declined, which increased after‑tax income [S4, S2].
  - Partly offsetting items: higher provision for credit losses (PCL total C$4,506m in 2025 vs C$4,253m in 2024) and continued insurance service expenses, but non‑interest expenses were lower overall (C$33,539m in 2025 vs C$35,493m in 2024) — these dynamics are in the segment table and notes [S3].
